1	# Working on Claude Sessions
2	
3	This app is used while it is being worked on. Dylan keeps a window open with
4	live sessions in it, and those sessions are real work in progress. The rules
5	below exist because breaking them destroys that work.
6	
7	## Never touch the everyday instance
8	
9	**Port 45888 belongs to the user.** Do not start a bridge on it, do not
10	`pkill -f bridge/server.js`, and do not `Stop-Process` ClaudeSessions.
11	
12	Use your own instance instead:
13	
14	```bash
15	npm run dev            # bridge on 45899 (or the next free port) + a window
16	npm run dev:headless   # bridge only; open the printed URL in a browser
17	```
18	
19	`npm run dev` refuses to bind 45888 and picks a free port near 45899, so two
20	agents can each have one. The window it opens is titled `dev :45899` and carries
21	an amber badge, so it is never confused with the everyday one.
22	
23	`pkill -f bridge/server.js` matches *every* bridge including the user's. If you
24	must stop your own, Ctrl-C the `npm run dev` you started, or kill it by port:
25	
26	```bash
27	kill "$(ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | grep :45899 | grep -oP 'pid=\K\d+' | head -1)"
28	```
29	
30	**`CLAUDE_SESSIONS_PORT` in your environment is not a port you chose.** A session
31	started from the app inherits the bridge's environment, so for a long time that
32	variable arrived pre-set to `45888` — and `bash bridge/launch.sh` or
33	`node bridge/server.js` from a worktree then bound the user's port without a port
34	ever being mentioned. That bridge reported `dev: false`, the Windows shell adopted
35	it in place of its own, and the everyday window quietly served a branch's UI out
36	of a stale worktree. It is the most expensive way this rule has been broken.
37	
38	Three things stop it now, and none of them is you remembering:
39	
40	- `bridge/server.js` refuses to bind 45888 when it is running out of
41	  `.claude/worktrees/` — exit 4, before the socket. `npm run dev` still refuses
42	  the port outright.
43	- The bridge no longer passes `CLAUDE_SESSIONS_PORT` to the sessions or terminals
44	  it starts, so a fresh session inherits nothing to trip over.
45	- `scripts/restart-bridge.sh` refuses the everyday port from a worktree. Without
46	  that it would kill the user's bridge and then fail to replace it, which is worse
47	  than the bug. `--status` still works from anywhere.
48	
49	`/api/health` reports `root` — which checkout a bridge is serving. When a window
50	shows something you cannot explain, check that first:
51	
52	```bash
53	curl -s http://127.0.0.1:45888/api/health | python3 -m json.tool | grep root
54	```
55	
56	## Work in a worktree, never the main checkout
57	
58	Several agents work on this repo at once — there are usually a handful of live
59	worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` — and they all reach for the same few files
60	in `bridge/` and `web/`. Editing `/home/dylan_hays/Other/claude-sessions`
61	directly means two agents silently overwriting each other, and it leaves the
62	user's own checkout dirty while they are running the app out of it.
63	
64	**Make the worktree your first action, before the first edit.** Use
65	`EnterWorktree` with a short name for the work; it branches `worktree-<name>` off
66	HEAD and moves you there.
67	
68	- **`cd` into the repo first.** `EnterWorktree` needs a git repository at the
69	  working directory; an agent launched in `~` reports "not in a git repository
70	  and no WorktreeCreate hooks are configured", which looks like a missing hook
71	  but is just the wrong directory.
72	- `baseRef` is pinned to `head` in `.claude/settings.json` because this repo has
73	  no remote — there is no `origin/main` to branch from.
74	- **Enter it before you start editing, not after.** Moving mid-session works, but
75	  every edit you have already made stays behind in the main checkout and has to
76	  be carried across by hand — which is a merge you did not need to do.
77	- Either way, a session that enters a worktree ends up with two transcript files.
78	  That is expected and handled; see *Notes that save time* for what it means.
79	- A dev bridge run from inside the worktree serves that worktree's `bridge/` and
80	  `web/`, which is what you want when verifying your own change.
81	
82	Not everything is an edit. Reading transcripts, diagnosing, querying a bridge and
83	running `npm run dev` are fine from wherever you are. The rule is about writing
84	to tracked files: if you are about to change one, be in a worktree. When in
85	doubt, make one — it costs a second and nothing is lost by it.
86	
87	## Clean up the sessions you start
88	
89	Every session you start to try something out lands in the user's sidebar, because
90	both instances read the same `~/.claude/projects`. Groups full of `probe`,
91	`sandbox` and the like are what that looks like after a few agents have been
92	through. **Do not leave them there.** Either:
93	
94	- **Mark it a test session**, which keeps it out of the everyday window entirely.
95	  Tick *Test session — dev only* in the Start a session dialog, or pass the field:
96	
97	  ```bash
98	  curl -sX POST http://127.0.0.1:45899/api/sessions \
99	    -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/.local/share/claude-sessions/token)" \
100	    -H 'X-Claude-Sessions-Client: 1' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
101	    -d '{"cwd":"'"$PWD"'","prompt":"…","test":true}'
102	  ```
103	
104	  Labelled sessions collect in a **Test sessions** card at the foot of the rail on
105	  dev only. Prefer this: a session you forget to delete is then still invisible to
106	  the user.
107	
108	- **Or delete it when you are done**, with the trash icon on the row, or:
109	
110	  ```bash
111	  curl -sX DELETE http://127.0.0.1:45899/api/sessions/$ID \
112	    -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/.local/share/claude-sessions/token)" \
113	    -H 'X-Claude-Sessions-Client: 1'
114	  ```
115	
116	  This is a hard delete — the transcript and its sidecar directory. Do it to
117	  sessions *you* created, never to one you found.
118	
119	  If the session's process is still shutting down, the exiting `claude` can write
120	  its bookkeeping back to the path you just unlinked, and the session reappears as
121	  an empty row with 0 turns. Stop it, wait a moment, then delete — or delete twice.
122	
123	Best is both: label it on the way in, delete it on the way out.
124	
125	## The API needs a token now
126	
127	Every `/api/` route but `/api/health` requires the token at
128	`~/.local/share/claude-sessions/token`, created on first run with mode `0600`. So
129	any `curl` against the bridge needs:
130	
131	```bash
132	-H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/.local/share/claude-sessions/token)"
133	```
134	
135	Without it you get `401 {"error":"unauthorized"}`, which is easy to misread as a
136	broken bridge.
137	
138	**Nothing in `web/` had to change for this, and nor should yours.** A page fetched
139	over loopback is served with the token in a `<meta name="cs-token">` tag *and* with
140	an `HttpOnly` cookie set; `fetch` and `EventSource` both send same-origin cookies
141	on their own. So the browser and the Electron shell need no login step, and the
142	service worker keeps working. Loopback is not otherwise trusted — "any process on
143	this machine" is the hole the token closes.
144	
145	`/api/health` stays open because `app/main.js` pings it before it could know a
146	token. It reports `remote`, which is what raises the banner in the UI.
147	
148	The bridge also refuses to bind a non-loopback interface without
149	`CLAUDE_SESSIONS_ALLOW_REMOTE_BIND=1`, and refuses several routes outright to
150	remote callers. See `docs/remote.md` for the reasoning and `docs/api.md` for the
151	contract.
152	
153	## Never rebuild without asking
154	
155	`install.ps1` force-closes any running ClaudeSessions and replaces the
156	executable, which shuts the user's window. You almost never need it: **changes
157	to `bridge/` and `web/` need no rebuild at all** — restart your dev bridge, or
158	just refresh for UI-only edits. Only `app/main.js` and `package.json` are
159	packaged, and if one of those has to ship, say so and let the user run it.
160	
161	Two agents packaging at once will also pull the executable out from under each
162	other, since the staging directory is wiped and rebuilt.
163	
164	## What is safe
165	
166	- Editing anything under `bridge/`, `web/`, `scripts/`.
167	- Running `npm run dev` and restarting it as often as you like.
168	- Reading transcripts: both instances read the same `~/.claude/projects`, so a
169	  session you start in dev is visible in the everyday window and vice versa.
170	
171	## Notes that save time
172	
173	- **Entering a worktree splits the session's transcript in two.** Claude Code
174	  files a transcript under the project directory for the cwd it is running in,
175	  and a worktree is a project directory of its own, so a session that crosses
176	  into one leaves a second `<id>.jsonl` under
177	  `~/.claude/projects/…--claude-worktrees-<name>/`. One copy holds the
178	  conversation and the other only bookkeeping — a title, a mode, the worktree
179	  state — and which gets which goes either way: both orders exist on this
180	  machine. `conversationRecord` in `bridge/sessions.js` is what picks the copy
181	  with the conversation in it. Before that the index took whichever copy was
182	  scanned last, so directory order decided whether a session showed its history
183	  or showed 0 turns and nothing at all.
184	- **No `node_modules`, on purpose.** `electron .` will not work here; the shell
185	  is packaged from a Windows-side staging directory. `npm start` finds the built
186	  executable instead.
187	- **A login shell has neither node nor `claude` on PATH** — nvm and `~/.local/bin`
188	  both come from `~/.bashrc`, which `bash -lc` never reads. `bridge/launch.sh`
189	  resolves node itself; that is why it exists.
190	- **Killing a bridge kills its turns.** This is measured, not assumed: `claude`
191	  reads stdin for input, so when the bridge exits and that pipe closes it treats
192	  it as end-of-input and stops, mid-turn. Running it detached with its output on
193	  a file descriptor does not change this. There is no way to make a turn outlive
194	  its bridge, which is the whole reason for the separate development port.
195

=== commit bodies (last 6, full) ===
--- Give each session its own terminal pane
The pane was a property of the window: open it once and every session you
moved to had a shell under it, including the ones you never wanted one in.
Remember the open flag against the session instead, the way a draft is
remembered — a session with no answer of its own starts closed.

The height stays window-wide. That part of the old reasoning still holds,
and a pane that resized itself as you moved between sessions would be worse
than one that did not.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

--- Start a session somewhere you have never worked
The directory list came from index.projects(), which is derived from
transcripts already on disk — so a folder this app had never seen never
appeared in it, and a folder that did not exist yet was unreachable
entirely. The only way in was knowing the absolute path and typing it.

Most of the bridge for this was already written and had never been
called. GET /api/fs lists directories, is scoped to the same roots a
session may start in, and stops "up" at their edge; its section header
in server.js literally reads "new-session directory picker". It is
documented and tested. No client ever asked it for anything. This wires
up the picker it was built for.

Recent and Browse are two tabs over one decision, and the rule that
keeps them from fighting is that walking into a folder IS choosing it.
There is no select-versus-descend distinction and no checkmark: every
navigation writes #new-cwd, which stays the single answer to "where will
this run". So "how do I pick the folder I am looking at?" answers
itself — you already have, and the box above says so. An empty folder
says the same thing in words, at the moment somebody standing in one
thinks to ask.

POST /api/fs/mkdir is the one route that was missing. Its body is
{parent, name} rather than a joined path, which is the whole safety
argument: a name can then be refused outright for containing a
separator, instead of being sanitised afterwards and hoping nothing was
missed. It makes one directory, never a chain — the picker can navigate,
so nesting would add path-parsing surface to buy something the UI
already does, and a non-recursive mkdir keeps EEXIST meaningful. A
leading dot is refused because listDir hides dotfiles, so such a folder
would vanish from the very pane that made it.

It is refused for remote callers, on the exact path rather than the
/api/fs prefix. The asymmetry is deliberate and is the interesting part:
reading the tree answers "where could a session start", and a phone may
already start one. Writing to the filesystem is reaching past the app
into the machine, which is the line docs/remote.md draws.

listDir gains three things the pane needs. It now follows symlinks that
point at directories — readdir reports isDirectory() false for those, so
a project tree linked into place was simply invisible before. It returns
the roots, so a breadcrumb knows where the trail stops and what to call
the top of it. And it says when the 500 cap bit, which used to be silent
and therefore read as "this is all of it".

Desktop only. mobile.js keeps its recents select and the comment
explaining why browsing a tree on a phone is the wrong shape for that
input.

## Working on this with agents

`.claude/settings.json` pins `worktree.baseRef` to `head`. The global default is
`fresh`, which branches a new worktree from `origin/<default-branch>` — and this
repo has no remote, so there is no `origin/master` to branch from. Pinning it to
the local HEAD avoids that whole question. Add a remote later and either setting
works.

Two other things that trip agents up here:

- **Start them in this directory.** `EnterWorktree` needs a git repository at the
  working directory. An agent launched in `~` reports "not in a git repository
  and no WorktreeCreate hooks are configured", which reads like a missing hook
  but is really just the wrong cwd. Nothing needs configuring — `cd` here first.
- **One build at a time.** `install.ps1` wipes and rebuilds its staging
  directory, so two agents packaging at once will pull the executable out from
  under each other.

- **Reasoning is usually blank.** Claude Code writes the signature of a thinking
  block but strips its text — across the 6,898 blocks on this machine only 29
  kept any. Newer sessions do keep it, and those render; older ones show nothing
  because there is nothing there.

  session is resumable. For a few seconds afterwards the button reads **Force
  stop**, which kills the process — the old behaviour, and still the thing to
  reach for when the polite path does not take. The status line says which one
  happened, because the outcomes differ.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Restart the everyday bridge so it picks up whatever is on main now.
#
#   restart-bridge              restart from the local checkout
#   restart-bridge --pull       fast-forward from origin first, then restart
#   restart-bridge --force      restart even with a turn in flight
#   restart-bridge --status     say what is running and exit
#
# Deliberately narrow: it only ever touches the instance on the everyday port.
# `pkill -f bridge/server.js` would match development bridges too, and killing
# one of those out from under an agent is the thing this whole setup avoids.

set -uo pipefail

PORT="${CLAUDE_SESSIONS_PORT:-45888}"
REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
LOG_DIR="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/claude-sessions"
LOG="$LOG_DIR/bridge-$PORT.log"

PULL=0; FORCE=0; STATUS_ONLY=0
for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --pull) PULL=1 ;;
        --force) FORCE=1 ;;
        --status) STATUS_ONLY=1 ;;
        -h|--help) sed -n '3,12p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "restart-bridge: unknown option '$arg'" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
done

health() { curl -fsS -m 3 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/api/health" 2>/dev/null; }

# Read one field out of the health JSON without needing jq.
field() {
    python3 -c "import json,sys
try: print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('$1',''))
except Exception: print('')" 2>/dev/null
}

CURRENT="$(health)"

if [ "$STATUS_ONLY" = 1 ]; then
    if [ -z "$CURRENT" ]; then
        echo "bridge :$PORT  not running"
    else
        # A bridge older than the `busy` field reports nothing for it; say so
        # rather than printing a hole.
        BUSY="$(printf '%s' "$CURRENT" | field busy)"
        printf 'bridge :%s  pid %s  %s sessions  %s client(s)  %s turn(s) in flight\n' \
            "$PORT" "$(printf '%s' "$CURRENT" | field pid)" \
            "$(printf '%s' "$CURRENT" | field sessions)" \
            "$(printf '%s' "$CURRENT" | field clients)" \
            "${BUSY:-an unknown number of}"
    fi
    exit 0
fi

# --- never the everyday instance, from a worktree ---------------------------

# This script kills whatever is on $PORT and starts a bridge from $REPO — the
# checkout it lives in. Run from a worktree against the everyday port, that
# replaces the user's bridge with a branch's, which is the failure the port guard
# in bridge/server.js exists to stop. And because that guard now refuses the
# bind, the replacement would never come up: the everyday instance would be dead
# rather than merely wrong. So refuse here, before anything is killed.
#
# --status is read-only and stays allowed above.
case "$REPO/" in
    */.claude/worktrees/*)
        if [ "$PORT" = 45888 ]; then
            echo "restart-bridge: $REPO is a worktree." >&2
            echo "  Refusing to restart the everyday bridge on $PORT — it would come" >&2
            echo "  back serving this worktree, and bridge/server.js will not allow that." >&2
            echo "  Your own: CLAUDE_SESSIONS_PORT=45899 scripts/restart-bridge.sh" >&2
            echo "  The everyday one: run this from the main checkout." >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        ;;
esac

# --- don't throw away work -------------------------------------------------

if [ -n "$CURRENT" ]; then
    BUSY="$(printf '%s' "$CURRENT" | field busy)"
    if [ -n "$BUSY" ] && [ "$BUSY" != "0" ] && [ "$FORCE" != 1 ]; then
        echo "restart-bridge: $BUSY turn(s) still running." >&2
        echo "  A restart ends them — Claude stops when its input pipe closes." >&2
        echo "  Wait for them, or re-run with --force if you don't mind." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
fi

# --- optionally catch up with the remote -----------------------------------

if [ "$PULL" = 1 ]; then
    echo "Updating $REPO…"
    # --ff-only so this can never leave a merge or a conflict behind; if the
    # branch has diverged, that is a decision for a human.
    if ! git -C "$REPO" pull --ff-only; then
        echo "restart-bridge: pull failed, leaving the bridge alone." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
fi

# --- say what is about to be loaded ----------------------------------------

# The bridge runs what is on disk, not what is committed. On a repo where
# several agents work at once that regularly means somebody's half-finished
# edits, so name them rather than loading them silently.
DIRTY="$(git -C "$REPO" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^??' | wc -l)"
if [ "${DIRTY:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "Heads up: $DIRTY tracked file(s) in $REPO have uncommitted changes."
    git -C "$REPO" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^??' | sed 's/^/    /'
    echo "  The bridge loads what is on disk, so it will run these too."
    if [ "$FORCE" != 1 ]; then
        printf '  Continue? [y/N] '
        read -r reply </dev/tty 2>/dev/null || reply=n
        case "$reply" in
            [yY]*) ;;
            *) echo "Left the bridge alone."; exit 1 ;;
        esac
    fi
fi

# --- swap it out -----------------------------------------------------------

if [ -n "$CURRENT" ]; then
    PID="$(printf '%s' "$CURRENT" | field pid)"
    OLD_REV="$(printf '%s' "$CURRENT" | field version)"
    if [ -n "$PID" ]; then
        kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null
        for _ in $(seq 1 25); do
            health >/dev/null 2>&1 || break
            sleep 0.2
        done
    fi
    echo "Stopped pid $PID."
else
    echo "Nothing was listening on $PORT."
fi

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
cd "$REPO" || exit 1
# setsid so it is its own session: it outlives this shell, and a stray signal
# aimed at the terminal cannot reach it.
setsid nohup bash bridge/launch.sh >"$LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null &
disown 2>/dev/null || true

for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
    sleep 0.5
    NEW="$(health)"
    [ -n "$NEW" ] && break
done

if [ -z "${NEW:-}" ]; then
    echo "restart-bridge: it did not come back. Last output:" >&2
    tail -n 20 "$LOG" >&2
    exit 1
fi

printf 'Bridge :%s up — pid %s, %s sessions, running %s\n' \
    "$PORT" "$(printf '%s' "$NEW" | field pid)" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$NEW" | field sessions)" \
    "$(git -C "$REPO" log --oneline -1 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-60)"

# The window reconnects on its own; say so, because a blank moment looks broken.
echo 'Any open window reconnects by itself.'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Land the branch you have been working on: merge its pull request, then bring
# the main checkout up to date with what you just merged.
#
#   land                   merge the PR for this branch, then pull the main checkout
#   land --branch NAME     land a branch other than the one you are standing on
#   land --squash          squash instead of a merge commit (--rebase also works)
#   land --delete-branch   delete the remote branch afterwards
#   land --no-pull         merge only, leave the main checkout alone
#   land --restart         also restart the everyday bridge (opt-in; see below)
#   land --dry-run         say what would happen and change nothing
#   land --status          report what is landable here and exit
#
# Why this exists. An agent finishes in a worktree, pushes, and opens a PR — and
# then the work sits on origin while the checkout the user actually runs the app
# from knows nothing about it. Closing that gap by hand is three commands, one of
# which an agent is not allowed to run: a worktree-isolated session is refused
# `git -C <the main checkout>` by its own harness, because pointing git at a
# directory computed at runtime is how agents commit to the wrong tree. This
# script is the sanctioned way through. It is deliberately narrow so that being
# sanctioned is safe: it fast-forwards and nothing else, it will not touch a main
# checkout that is dirty or on another branch, and it never commits there.
#
# It does not restart the bridge unless asked. The everyday instance usually has
# live turns in it and a restart ends them — `claude` stops when its input pipe
# closes — so picking up merged code is the user's call, not a side effect of
# landing a branch. What the merge implies is printed instead.

set -uo pipefail

# Where the user actually runs the app from. Overridable, but this is the
# answer on this machine and the default is what makes the script callable
# from a worktree that cannot know it.
MAIN="${CLAUDE_SESSIONS_MAIN:-$HOME/Other/claude-sessions}"
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

METHOD=--merge
BRANCH=""; PULL=1; RESTART=0; DRY=0; STATUS_ONLY=0; DELETE=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --branch) shift; BRANCH="${1:-}" ;;
        --branch=*) BRANCH="${1#*=}" ;;
        --squash) METHOD=--squash ;;
        --rebase) METHOD=--rebase ;;
        --merge) METHOD=--merge ;;
        --delete-branch) DELETE=1 ;;
        --no-pull) PULL=0 ;;
        --restart) RESTART=1 ;;
        --dry-run) DRY=1 ;;
        --status) STATUS_ONLY=1 ;;
        -h|--help) sed -n '3,16p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "land: unknown option '$1'" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    shift
done

say() { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
die() { printf 'land: %s\n' "$1" >&2; shift; for l in "$@"; do printf '  %s\n' "$l" >&2; done; exit 1; }

# --- what are we landing ----------------------------------------------------

[ -n "$BRANCH" ] || BRANCH="$(git -C "$HERE" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null)"
[ -n "$BRANCH" ] && [ "$BRANCH" != HEAD ] || die "could not work out which branch to land." \
    "Pass one: land --branch <name>"

DEFAULT_BRANCH="$(git -C "$HERE" symbolic-ref --quiet --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's|^origin/||')"
[ -n "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" ] || DEFAULT_BRANCH=main

if [ "$BRANCH" = "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" ]; then
    die "you are on $DEFAULT_BRANCH." \
        "There is nothing to land: this is the branch things land onto." \
        "Run this from the worktree whose work you want merged."
fi

# --- is the branch actually finished ---------------------------------------

# Merging a PR that does not include the edits still sitting in the working tree
# is the quiet way to lose them: the branch merges, the agent moves on, and the
# uncommitted half is only noticed later. Refuse rather than warn.
DIRTY="$(git -C "$HERE" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | grep -cv '^??')"
if [ "${DIRTY:-0}" -gt 0 ] && [ "$STATUS_ONLY" != 1 ]; then
    git -C "$HERE" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^??' | sed 's/^/    /' >&2
    die "$DIRTY tracked file(s) here are not committed." \
        "They are not in the PR, so landing it now would leave them behind." \
        "Commit them and push, or stash them deliberately, then run this again."
fi

UNPUSHED="$(git -C "$HERE" rev-list --count "origin/$BRANCH..$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
if [ "$UNPUSHED" = unknown ]; then
    [ "$STATUS_ONLY" = 1 ] || die "$BRANCH has never been pushed." \
        "Push it first: git push -u origin $BRANCH"
elif [ "${UNPUSHED:-0}" -gt 0 ] && [ "$STATUS_ONLY" != 1 ]; then
    die "$BRANCH is $UNPUSHED commit(s) ahead of origin/$BRANCH." \
        "The PR would merge without them. Push first: git push"
fi

# --- find the pull request --------------------------------------------------

PR_JSON="$(gh pr view "$BRANCH" --json number,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,title,url 2>/dev/null)"
if [ -z "$PR_JSON" ]; then
    die "no pull request found for $BRANCH." \
        "Open one first — the title and body are yours to write:" \
        "  gh pr create --head $BRANCH --fill"
fi

field() {
    printf '%s' "$PR_JSON" | python3 -c "import json,sys
try: print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('$1',''))
except Exception: print('')" 2>/dev/null
}

PR_NUM="$(field number)"; PR_STATE="$(field state)"; PR_TITLE="$(field title)"
PR_URL="$(field url)"; MERGEABLE="$(field mergeable)"; MERGE_STATE="$(field mergeStateStatus)"

if [ "$STATUS_ONLY" = 1 ]; then
    say "branch      $BRANCH"
    say "pull request #$PR_NUM  $PR_STATE  $PR_TITLE"
    say "            $PR_URL"
    say "mergeable   $MERGEABLE ($MERGE_STATE)"
    say "unpushed    ${UNPUSHED:-0} commit(s)"
    say "uncommitted ${DIRTY:-0} tracked file(s)"
    say "main        $MAIN"
    exit 0
fi

[ "$PR_STATE" = OPEN ] || die "PR #$PR_NUM is $PR_STATE, not OPEN." "$PR_URL"

if [ "$MERGEABLE" = CONFLICTING ]; then
    die "PR #$PR_NUM conflicts with $DEFAULT_BRANCH." \
        "Merge $DEFAULT_BRANCH into $BRANCH and resolve it, then run this again." \
        "$PR_URL"
fi

case "$MERGE_STATE" in
    BLOCKED|DIRTY)
        die "PR #$PR_NUM is not mergeable yet — $MERGE_STATE." \
            "Failing checks or an unmet review rule. Look before forcing it:" \
            "$PR_URL" ;;
esac

# --- merge ------------------------------------------------------------------

say "Landing #$PR_NUM — $PR_TITLE"
MERGE_ARGS=("$PR_NUM" "$METHOD")
[ "$DELETE" = 1 ] && MERGE_ARGS+=(--delete-branch)

if [ "$DRY" = 1 ]; then
    say "  would run: gh pr merge ${MERGE_ARGS[*]}"
else
    if ! gh pr merge "${MERGE_ARGS[@]}"; then
        die "gh pr merge failed. Nothing was pulled." "$PR_URL"
    fi
    say "Merged."
fi

# --- bring the main checkout up to date ------------------------------------

if [ "$PULL" != 1 ]; then
    say "Left $MAIN alone (--no-pull)."
    exit 0
fi

[ -d "$MAIN/.git" ] || die "no main checkout at $MAIN." \
    "Set CLAUDE_SESSIONS_MAIN if it lives somewhere else." \
    "The merge is done; only the pull was skipped."

MAIN_BRANCH="$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null)"
if [ "$MAIN_BRANCH" != "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" ]; then
    say "Heads up: $MAIN is on '$MAIN_BRANCH', not $DEFAULT_BRANCH — not pulling."
    say "  The merge is done. Pull it yourself once that checkout is back on $DEFAULT_BRANCH."
    exit 0
fi

MAIN_DIRTY="$(git -C "$MAIN" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | grep -cv '^??')"
if [ "${MAIN_DIRTY:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    git -C "$MAIN" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^??' | sed 's/^/    /'
    say "Heads up: $MAIN has ${MAIN_DIRTY} uncommitted tracked file(s) — not pulling."
    say "  The merge is done. Deal with those, then: git -C $MAIN pull --ff-only"
    exit 0
fi

BEFORE="$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)"

if [ "$DRY" = 1 ]; then
    say "  would run: git -C $MAIN pull --ff-only"
    exit 0
fi

say "Updating $MAIN…"
# --ff-only so this can never leave a merge or a conflict in the checkout the
# user is working out of. A diverged main is a decision for a human.
if ! git -C "$MAIN" pull --ff-only; then
    die "pull failed in $MAIN — it has probably diverged from origin." \
        "The merge is done; sort the checkout out by hand."
fi

AFTER="$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)"

# --- say what that means ----------------------------------------------------

if [ "$BEFORE" = "$AFTER" ]; then
    say "$MAIN was already up to date."
    exit 0
fi

CHANGED="$(git -C "$MAIN" diff --name-only "$BEFORE" "$AFTER" 2>/dev/null)"
say "$MAIN is now at $(git -C "$MAIN" log --oneline -1 | cut -c1-60)"

# The bridge runs what was on disk when it started, so a merge that touched
# bridge/ is on disk but not in the running process. Say so; do not act on it.
if printf '%s\n' "$CHANGED" | grep -q '^bridge/'; then
    say ""
    say "This merge changed bridge/ — the running bridge is still on the old code."
    if [ "$RESTART" != 1 ]; then
        say "  When it suits you, from $MAIN:  npm run restart"
        say "  (it refuses while a turn is in flight, which is the point)"
    fi
fi
if printf '%s\n' "$CHANGED" | grep -qE '^(app/|package\.json)'; then
    say ""
    say "This merge changed app/ or package.json — the packaged shell is stale."
    say "  That needs a rebuild, which closes the user's window: npm run build"
    say "  Ask before running it."
fi
if printf '%s\n' "$CHANGED" | grep -q '^web/' \
   && ! printf '%s\n' "$CHANGED" | grep -q '^bridge/'; then
    say ""
    say "This merge was UI only — a refresh in the open window picks it up."
fi

# --- optionally restart, having been asked explicitly -----------------------

if [ "$RESTART" = 1 ]; then
    say ""
    say "Restarting the everyday bridge, as asked…"
    # Delegated rather than reimplemented: that script has the turn-in-flight
    # guard, and running it from $MAIN is the one place it is allowed to
    # replace the everyday instance.
    ( cd "$MAIN" && bash scripts/restart-bridge.sh )
fi

An agent finishes in a worktree, pushes, opens a PR — and the work then sits

nothing about it. Closing that gap was three commands, and one of them an
agent is not allowed to run: a worktree-isolated session is refused

tree. That refusal is right, so the answer is a sanctioned path rather than
an exception.

fast-forwards ~/Other/claude-sessions. It is narrow so that being sanctioned
is safe: --ff-only and nothing else, never a commit, and it will not touch a
main checkout that is dirty or on another branch — it reports and stops.

It refuses rather than guesses, and the refusals are the substance of it.

merges, the agent moves on, and the half that was never committed is noticed
later, so that one is a refusal and not a warning. Unpushed commits are the
same failure a step earlier. Beyond that: a PR that conflicts, a PR that is
BLOCKED, a main checkout that has diverged. Anything that fails after the
merge says the merge happened, so it is always clear which half landed.

instance usually has live turns in it and a restart ends them — `claude`
stops when its input pipe closes — so picking up merged code is a decision
someone makes, not a side effect of landing a branch. What the merge implies

package.json means the packaged shell is stale and needs a rebuild that would
close the user's window, web/ alone means a refresh is enough. --restart opts
